newContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Shout About Us: Technical Account Manager, API Partnerships Anywhere in the World California API, Client Relationship Management, Communication Skills, Relationship Building, and REST APIs Customer Support Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6493/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> San Diego, CA, USA <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="http://www.shoutaboutus.com">http://www.shoutaboutus.com</a> </p> <h2>Technical Account Manager, API Partnerships</h2> <p>Shout About Us · Remote (worldwide) · Full-time · 60K - 80K USD</p> <h2>About the role</h2> <p>We're hiring a Technical Account Manager to own and grow our most strategic accounts. You’ll own the technical relationship with our API partners, from their first technical evaluation through implementation and ongoing support.</p> <p>Reporting directly to the CRO, you’ll be the first dedicated post-sales professional at Shout About Us, responsible for making sure our biggest customers deploy, expand, and stay. Our ICP is founders, product teams, and engineering teams.&nbsp;</p> <p>This is a hands-on role. On any given day, you might join a prospect’s technical discovery call, troubleshoot an API request with a partner engineer, coordinate a fix with our engineering team, or improve a quickstart guide. You’ll also help build the documentation and processes that make each new integration easier than the last.</p> <h2>Location and hours</h2> <p>Remote, anywhere. Our standard working hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. US Eastern Time, including a lunch break. Occasional calls outside these hours are required for APAC partners and key implementation milestones.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Own a portfolio of 10-15 strategic accounts. Be the primary technical contact for API partners, keep stakeholders informed, and follow issues through to resolution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Support technical evaluations. Join sales calls, demonstrate API capabilities, understand the partner’s requirements, and explain how an integration would work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead partner implementations. Turn requirements into a clear integration plan, guide developers through setup and testing, and track progress through launch.</p> </li> <li> <p>Troubleshoot directly. Investigate requests, responses, logs, authentication issues, and integration behavior before escalating to engineering.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work closely with engineering. Provide clear reproduction steps, relevant evidence, and customer impact when an issue needs deeper investigation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve the developer experience. Create and maintain API guides, Postman collections, code examples, FAQs, and onboarding playbooks.</p> </li> <li> <p>Identify recurring friction. Share partner feedback and integration patterns that can inform product improvements.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead expansion efforts. Cross-sell new features and products as a natural extension of the relationship, not a separate motion.&nbsp;</p> </li> </ul> <h2>What we’re looking for</h2> <ul> <li> <p>4+ years in a customer-facing technical role or equivalent at an API-first or dev-tools company</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong practical understanding of REST APIs, HTTP, JSON, authentication, webhooks, pagination, and rate limits.</p> </li> <li> <p>Comfort using Postman or curl, reading logs, and writing or adapting small code examples in a language such as JavaScript or Python.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience driving adoption inside complex orgs: navigating the gap between the buyer who signed and the team that deploys</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong follow-through. You keep track of open questions, set expectations, and make sure customers know what happens next.</p> </li> <li> <p>Startup experience at a company under 50 people. There's no support team behind you.</p> </li> <li> <p>Clear written and spoken English. You can explain the same issue to a developer and a nontechnical stakeholder.</p> </li> <li> <p>Owner mentality. "I'll make sure this gets done," not "I passed it to engineering."</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Why you should join</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Own meaningful partner relationships from technical evaluation through launch and beyond.</p> </li> <li> <p>See the impact of your work in successful integrations and better customer experiences.</p> </li> <li> <p>You’ll own and drive every initiative you work on from start to finish. We fully trust you.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work remotely from anywhere while collaborating on a shared schedule.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work directly with the people selling and building the product.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Why you shouldn't join</p> <ul> <li> <p>You are not comfortable working without a clear structure and playbook.&nbsp;</p> </li> <li> <p>You need predictable hours. Most weeks are normal. Go-live weeks and APAC escalations aren't.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Interview process</p> <p>Our process includes an introductory call, a short written exercise, a practical technical session, and a final conversation with our CEO. We’ll share the details and expected time commitment before each step.</p> <h2>About Shout About Us</h2> <p>Shout About Us is API-first review infrastructure for marketplaces and platforms.</p> <p>Reviews are the most valuable decision signal in every transaction: which agent, which contractor, which property, which restaurant. Almost every platform that hosts those decisions rents that signal from Google, Trustpilot or Yelp. We give platforms the APIs and infrastructure to own it.</p> <p>What you can build with our APIs:</p> <ul> <li> <p>A verified first-party review engine: collection, verification, moderation and publishing under your brand</p> </li> <li> <p>Third-party review aggregation from Google, Yelp, Facebook and 80+ other sources</p> </li> <li> <p>AI review responses drafted and posted natively, without your customers leaving your platform</p> </li> <li> <p>Review solicitation and surveys triggered from events in your product</p> </li> <li> <p>Flagging, disputes, AI insight reports and competitor analysis</p> </li> </ul> <p>We’re a small team looking for someone who can make it easier for partners to understand, integrate, and succeed with our API.</p> <p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/shout-about-us-technical-account-manager-api-partnerships">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/shout-about-us-technical-account-manager-api-partnerships</a></p> Tue, 29 Sep 2026 23:00:15 +0000 Thu, 29 Oct 2026 23:00:15 +0000 https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/shout-about-us-technical-account-manager-api-partnerships https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/shout-about

oldContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Shout About Us: Technical Account Manager, API Partnerships Anywhere in the World California API, Client Relationship Management, Communication Skills, Relationship Building, and REST APIs Customer Support Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6493/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> San Diego, CA, USA <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="http://www.shoutaboutus.com">http://www.shoutaboutus.com</a> </p> <h2>Technical Account Manager, API Partnerships</h2> <p>Shout About Us · Remote (worldwide) · Full-time · 60K - 80K USD</p> <h2>About the role</h2> <p>We're hiring a Technical Account Manager to own and grow our most strategic accounts. You’ll own the technical relationship with our API partners, from their first technical evaluation through implementation and ongoing support.</p> <p>Reporting directly to the CRO, you’ll be the first dedicated post-sales professional at Shout About Us, responsible for making sure our biggest customers deploy, expand, and stay. Our ICP is founders, product teams, and engineering teams.&nbsp;</p> <p>This is a hands-on role. On any given day, you might join a prospect’s technical discovery call, troubleshoot an API request with a partner engineer, coordinate a fix with our engineering team, or improve a quickstart guide. You’ll also help build the documentation and processes that make each new integration easier than the last.</p> <h2>Location and hours</h2> <p>Remote, anywhere. Our standard working hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. US Eastern Time, including a lunch break. Occasional calls outside these hours are required for APAC partners and key implementation milestones.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Own a portfolio of 10-15 strategic accounts. Be the primary technical contact for API partners, keep stakeholders informed, and follow issues through to resolution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Support technical evaluations. Join sales calls, demonstrate API capabilities, understand the partner’s requirements, and explain how an integration would work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead partner implementations. Turn requirements into a clear integration plan, guide developers through setup and testing, and track progress through launch.</p> </li> <li> <p>Troubleshoot directly. Investigate requests, responses, logs, authentication issues, and integration behavior before escalating to engineering.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work closely with engineering. Provide clear reproduction steps, relevant evidence, and customer impact when an issue needs deeper investigation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve the developer experience. Create and maintain API guides, Postman collections, code examples, FAQs, and onboarding playbooks.</p> </li> <li> <p>Identify recurring friction. Share partner feedback and integration patterns that can inform product improvements.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead expansion efforts. Oura had planned to offer 50 million shares at $40 to $44 apiece and was expected to begin trading Wednesday. At the top of that range, the offering would have raised $2.2 billion. The company says it is delaying the deal despite strong demand and has not set a new date. CEO Tom Hale said Oura has “the luxury of choosing our moment.” Anthropic is still moving toward an IPO, although its timing remains unclear. A prospectus leaked by Reuters showed that revenue climbed twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion in 2025 with an operating loss of $8.06 billion. Its staggering nearly $42 billion net loss included roughly $34 billion in accounting charges tied largely to earlier financing. The document also outlined an eye-watering $518 billion in future cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations. Anthropic, the world’s most valuable venture-backed startup, has indicated it plans to beat rival OpenAI to the public markets. The company could debut as soon as October and raise up to $100 billion via the offering, according to a recent report in The Wall Street Journal , while OpenAI, which Reuters says filed confidentially in June, is reportedly now looking toward early 2027. (Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence tools, meanwhile, point to a slightly longer timeline for an Anthropic IPO, saying it’s more likely to happen in six to 12 months.) Who’s next So far, the 2026 IPO class already has a record-setting headliner in SpaceX . There are some other candidates. Nvidia -backed AI cloud provider Nscale filed publicly this month for a U.S. listing , reporting $140.6 million in first-half revenue and a $1.02 billion net loss. The Fidelis Partnership , a Blackstone -backed specialty insurance underwriter, filed on Sept. 24. Neither has announced a trading date. Data center operator Switch is another possible fourth-quarter entrant. Reuters reported in July that it had hired banks for an IPO that could raise as much as $10 billion, although the timing remains subject to change. Her daughter had been born by C-section, while her younger son, born vaginally, had no similar conditions. The contrast made her wonder whether differences in their early microbial exposure played a role. While it did not give her a diagnosis for her daughter, it gave her an idea for a company. “I learned that you can course-correct if you focus on the early life of the baby. If they’re missing certain beneficial bacteria, it can really cause a lot of issues for the infant,” Sew Hoy recalls. “I was reading all this literature and asked my doctors about it, and none of my doctors knew what I was talking about.” Cheryl Sew Hoy, co-founder and CEO of Tiny Health. (Courtesy photo) A week after her son’s birth in 2020, she incorporated Austin-based Tiny Health . Today, the company announced it has raised $33 million in a Series B funding round led by B Capital , it told Crunchbase News exclusively. The financing brings Tiny Health’s total funding to $46 million, following a $4.5 million seed round in 2021 and an $8.5 million Series A in late 2023. Existing investors Spero Ventures , The Venture City and Overwater Ventures participated in the latest round, along with new investors including Black Opal Ventures and Alumni Ventures . B Capital’s Nick Whitehead will join the company’s board. Demand for Tiny Health’s at-home microbiome tests is growing. The startup’s overall revenue has more than doubled each year, according to Sew Hoy. Its B2B arm, Powered by Tiny, which sells tests through healthcare providers and other companies, grew fourfold last year. Sew Hoy did not disclose revenue figures or the company’s valuation, though she said the valuation was “much higher” than in the Series A. From baby gut tests to adult testing Tiny Health spent two years developing its platform before launching an at-home baby gut test in 2022. Healthcare was new territory for Sew Hoy, whose previous startup, digital coupon company Reclip.It , was sold to Walmart Labs in 2013. Before raising a seed round, she put $50,000 of her own money into an initial study and spent about a year collecting stool samples and building the platform. The baby test gave Tiny Health a focused entry point. In Sew Hoy’s view, parents of children with conditions such as eczema wanted more information as to the cause, while clinicians had few practical tools to apply emerging microbiome research. The company also offered pregnancy, vaginal microbiome and adult tests, but initially focused on infant testing. Adults have since become its larger testing segment, according to Sew Hoy. So, how does it work? Customers collect a small stool sample with a swab. After sending in the swab, they receive a report on the microbes detected, along with explanations and suggested next steps. Tiny Health also sells a subscription called Tiny Plus that includes a baseline test and a retest. Sew Hoy believes one of Tiny Health’s biggest differentiators is that its tests use shotgun metagenomic sequencing to analyze microbial DNA. The method provides a broader view of the organisms in a sample than tests that look for a limited set of microbes, she said. Chief science officer Kimberley Sukhum , who joined Tiny Health in 2021, leads its scientific work. The company’s other leaders include co-founder Donald Koo , who joined Sew Hoy two years after she started Tiny Health and leads its technology work, and chief medical officer Dr. Elisa Song , an integrative pediatrician who previously advised the company. Tiny Health’s PRO Gut Health Test kit. (Courtesy photo) The reports examine what the detected microbes may be doing and suggest steps such as dietary changes, with links to supporting research. “We are a wellness test,” Sew Hoy said. “We’re not a diagnostic … It’s very actionable, very evidence-backed.” Insurance does not cover the tests, which can identify microbes in a sample, but cannot establish what caused a person’s symptoms. Other startups are taking different approaches to digestive health. Austin-based Throne Science makes a device that attaches to a toilet and tracks stool patterns and hydration. Tiny Health analyzes microbial DNA from a collected sample. Throne recently raised $10 million in a Series A round led by Will Ventures . (Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence tools, meanwhile, point to a slightly longer timeline for an Anthropic IPO, saying it’s more likely to happen in six to 12 months.) Who’s next So far, the 2026 IPO class already has a record-setting headliner in SpaceX . There are some other candidates. Nvidia -backed AI cloud provider Nscale filed publicly this month for a U.S. listing , reporting $140.6 million in first-half revenue and a $1.02 billion net loss. The Fidelis Partnership , a Blackstone -backed specialty insurance underwriter, filed on Sept. 24. Neither has announced a trading date. Data center operator Switch is another possible fourth-quarter entrant. Reuters reported in July that it had hired banks for an IPO that could raise as much as $10 billion, although the timing remains subject to change. Her daughter had been born by C-section, while her younger son, born vaginally, had no similar conditions. The contrast made her wonder whether differences in their early microbial exposure played a role. While it did not give her a diagnosis for her daughter, it gave her an idea for a company. “I learned that you can course-correct if you focus on the early life of the baby. (Courtesy photo) A week after her son’s birth in 2020, she incorporated Austin-based Tiny Health . Today, the company announced it has raised $33 million in a Series B funding round led by B Capital , it told Crunchbase News exclusively. The financing brings Tiny Health’s total funding to $46 million, following a $4.5 million seed round in 2021 and an $8.5 million Series A in late 2023. Existing investors Spero Ventures , The Venture City and Overwater Ventures participated in the latest round, along with new investors including Black Opal Ventures and Alumni Ventures . B Capital’s Nick Whitehead will join the company’s board. Demand for Tiny Health’s at-home microbiome tests is growing. The startup’s overall revenue has more than doubled each year, according to Sew Hoy. Its B2B arm, Powered by Tiny, which sells tests through healthcare providers and other companies, grew fourfold last year. Sew Hoy did not disclose revenue figures or the company’s valuation, though she said the valuation was “much higher” than in the Series A. From baby gut tests to adult testing Tiny Health spent two years developing its platform before launching an at-home baby gut test in 2022. Healthcare was new territory for Sew Hoy, whose previous startup, digital coupon company Reclip.It , was sold to Walmart Labs in 2013. Before raising a seed round, she put $50,000 of her own money into an initial study and spent about a year collecting stool samples and building the platform. The baby test gave Tiny Health a focused entry point. In Sew Hoy’s view, parents of children with conditions such as eczema wanted more information as to the cause, while clinicians had few practical tools to apply emerging microbiome research. The company also offered pregnancy, vaginal microbiome and adult tests, but initially focused on infant testing. Adults have since become its larger testing segment, according to Sew Hoy. So, how does it work? Customers collect a small stool sample with a swab. After sending in the swab, they receive a report on the microbes detected, along with explanations and suggested next steps. Tiny Health also sells a subscription called Tiny Plus that includes a baseline test and a retest. Sew Hoy believes one of Tiny Health’s biggest differentiators is that its tests use shotgun metagenomic sequencing to analyze microbial DNA. That programme took the brand to over a billion views a month and the 13th most-mentioned fashion brand on TikTok UK, and put thousands of creators on contract. </p> <p>We have now launched it as a business in its own right, selling guaranteed organic views with product placement to brands.</p> <p>This is how brands grow now. Celsius, Bloom, Cal AI and Polymarket became big because thousands of creators had the product in their videos at the same time.</p> <p>The business is at multi six-figures in its first month operating from inbound.
